variants.title: Start from the failure
variants.context: Start from the failure, not the pattern name: vocabulary mismatch suggests dense retrieval, a bounded reformulation, or HyDE; multi-part evidence suggests decomposition and rank fusion; long document structure suggests hierarchical retrieval; a mixed workload suggests a bounded router that can abstain.
variants.prompt: Users ask about “PTO” but documents say “annual leave”. Which pattern addresses this?
options: An agentic planner that decides its own search strategy per question.
Dense retrieval, a bounded reformulation, or HyDE to bridge the terms.
Hierarchical retrieval, routing to the right section of a long document.
optionFeedback: Complexity must answer a measured failure, and this one is a single language gap.
The query and source describe one idea in different terms.
Document structure is not the problem here; the wording is.
variants.explanation: Add the smallest mechanism that addresses one persistent gap.

variants.title: Start from the failure
variants.context: Start from the failure, not the pattern name: vocabulary mismatch suggests dense retrieval, a bounded reformulation, or HyDE; multi-part evidence suggests decomposition and rank fusion; long document structure suggests hierarchical retrieval; a mixed workload suggests a bounded router that can abstain.
variants.prompt: Questions need one clause from the contract and one from the addendum, and single queries keep finding only one. Which pattern?
options: HyDE, generating one answer-shaped passage to search with.
Bigger chunks, so both clauses can land inside one retrieved unit.
Decomposition into subqueries, then rank fusion over the lists.
optionFeedback: HyDE addresses vocabulary mismatch, not evidence split across two documents.
Bigger chunks dilute similarity and still do not span two separate documents.
Multi-part evidence needs each sub-intent visible to its own search.
variants.hint: How many distinct facts does the answer need?
variants.explanation: Decomposition and rank fusion keep each sub-intent visible.

variants.title: Start from the failure
variants.context: Start from the failure, not the pattern name: vocabulary mismatch suggests dense retrieval, a bounded reformulation, or HyDE; multi-part evidence suggests decomposition and rank fusion; long document structure suggests hierarchical retrieval; a mixed workload suggests a bounded router that can abstain.
variants.prompt: A team wants to make every query agentic because it sounds mature. What is the right stance?
options: Never route at all, since one fixed pipeline is easier to reason about.
Keep a simple baseline as control and add stages only for measured failures.
Agentic planning is strictly better, so it should be the default route.
optionFeedback: Routing earns its place when a mixed workload demands it, so a blanket ban is also unmeasured.
Advanced RAG is not a maturity ladder, and planning calls add latency, cost, and failure modes.
There is no universal upgrade, and each added stage must beat the baseline.
variants.hint: What must a new stage prove?
variants.explanation: Preserve a simple branch as a control so additional calls must prove their value.

variants.title: Run the pattern
variants.context: Every advanced pattern changes the same stages: represent the intent (original plus the bounded decomposition or hypothetical the pattern needs), retrieve independent policy-filtered lists, fuse and select evidence, then release, retry once, or stop with a typed abstention.
variants.prompt: A multi-query pipeline handles a question. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Retrieve independent, policy-filtered lists, each with its own ranking contract.
Represent the intent: keep the original question and create only the bounded subqueries the pattern requires.
Fuse ranks, deduplicate lineage, attach bounded parent context, and reserve room for independent sources.
Check required facts, authority, freshness, and contradictions; release, retry once, or stop with a typed abstention.

variants.hint: A typed abstention is safer than an unbounded search loop.

variants.title: Run the pattern
variants.context: Every advanced pattern changes the same stages: represent the intent (original plus the bounded decomposition or hypothetical the pattern needs), retrieve independent policy-filtered lists, fuse and select evidence, then release, retry once, or stop with a typed abstention.
variants.prompt: The first pass misses a required fact. Put the stages in order, including the bounded retry.

items.text: Fusion selected evidence that lacks a required fact.
One defined fallback runs; if evidence is still incomplete, the system abstains.
Independent lists were retrieved.
The intent was represented.

variants.explanation: Every composition multiplies the trace, evaluation, and failure states an operator must understand.

variants.title: Run the pattern
variants.context: Every advanced pattern changes the same stages: represent the intent (original plus the bounded decomposition or hypothetical the pattern needs), retrieve independent policy-filtered lists, fuse and select evidence, then release, retry once, or stop with a typed abstention.
variants.prompt: HyDE is used. Put the stages in order and note what the hypothetical is for.

items.text: Fuse and select real evidence; the hypothetical is discarded.
Represent the intent by generating a hypothetical answer-shaped passage as a search representation only.
Retrieve real corpus documents near that representation, under policy filters.
Release only from real, authorized evidence.

variants.hint: The hypothetical text is a hint, never evidence.
variants.explanation: HyDE text may contain false details and must never be cited.

variants.title: Reason about fusion
variants.context: Reciprocal rank fusion ignores raw score magnitudes: score(document) = Σ 1 / (60 + rank) across active lists. A document outside every active top list contributes nothing, regardless of the downstream reranker.
variants.prompt: A document appears in three of four active ranked lists. How many lists contribute to its RRF score?
variants.hint: Only lists where the document appears contribute.
variants.explanation: Three contributions of 1 ÷ (60 + rank); the fourth list adds nothing.

mistakes.feedback: A list where the document is absent contributes nothing.

variants.title: Reason about fusion
variants.context: Reciprocal rank fusion ignores raw score magnitudes: score(document) = Σ 1 / (60 + rank) across active lists. A document outside every active top list contributes nothing, regardless of the downstream reranker.
variants.prompt: Four lists each contribute a top-20 window. At most how many distinct candidates can enter the fused set?
variants.explanation: 4 × 20 = 80 distinct candidates at most; overlap reduces it. A deeper window can add distractors and reranking work.

mistakes.feedback: That is the constant in the formula, not a count.

variants.title: Reason about fusion
variants.context: Reciprocal rank fusion ignores raw score magnitudes: score(document) = Σ 1 / (60 + rank) across active lists. A document outside every active top list contributes nothing, regardless of the downstream reranker.
variants.prompt: A relevant document is outside every active top list. What is its RRF contribution?
variants.explanation: Zero: fusion cannot recover a source that no input retriever found, however good the reranker is.

mistakes.feedback: The constant does not apply to absent documents.

variants.title: Retrieve through the hierarchy
variants.context: Hierarchical retrieval narrows in steps: search document-level representations, then section summaries inside the selected documents, then answer-bearing leaves, then attach only the parent context needed. A missed parent makes every child unreachable.
variants.prompt: A clause inside a 300-page manual is needed. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Attach only the heading path or neighboring text needed to interpret each leaf.
Search headings or section summaries only inside the selected documents.
Search stable document-level representations to identify likely source families.
Retrieve answer-bearing paragraphs, tables, or code blocks inside the selected sections.

variants.hint: Evaluate recall at every narrowing step.
variants.explanation: A missed parent makes every relevant child below it unreachable.

variants.title: Retrieve through the hierarchy
variants.context: Hierarchical retrieval narrows in steps: search document-level representations, then section summaries inside the selected documents, then answer-bearing leaves, then attach only the parent context needed. A missed parent makes every child unreachable.
variants.prompt: Parent routing confidence is low. Put the steps in order, including the fallback.

items.text: A controlled broad-search fallback runs across leaves because routing confidence is low.
Document-level search returns weak matches.
Section search is attempted inside them.
Attach bounded parent context to whatever leaves survive.

variants.hint: Permit a controlled broad-search fallback when routing is uncertain.
variants.explanation: Measure parent recall, leaf recall, and final coverage separately.

variants.title: Retrieve through the hierarchy
variants.context: Hierarchical retrieval narrows in steps: search document-level representations, then section summaries inside the selected documents, then answer-bearing leaves, then attach only the parent context needed. A missed parent makes every child unreachable.
variants.prompt: Summaries helped route the search. Put the steps in order and note what gets cited.

items.text: Search section summaries within the selected documents.
Retrieve the real leaf passage.
Cite the real source span, not the generated summary that helped route retrieval.
Search document summaries.

variants.hint: Generated summaries are derived data, not source evidence.
variants.explanation: Version summaries with the source snapshot.

variants.title: Use hints honestly
variants.context: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer-shaped passage as a search representation; it must never be cited. Contextual retrieval adds document context to a chunk’s representation while preserving the original span for citation. Fusion cannot repair authorization, staleness, or poisoning.
variants.prompt: A HyDE passage was passed to the model as a source and cited in the answer. What went wrong?
options: The passage should have been embedded twice so its score was reliable.
The hypothetical is a search representation and must never be cited.
Nothing went wrong, because the passage was relevant to the question.
optionFeedback: Embedding count changes retrieval scores, not whether a generated passage is evidence.
HyDE changes retrieval input, not the evidence the answer stands on.
Relevance is not truth, and this passage was invented rather than retrieved.
variants.hint: What trust promise does HyDE make?
variants.explanation: Use generated representations as search hints, never as evidence.

variants.title: Use hints honestly
variants.context: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer-shaped passage as a search representation; it must never be cited. Contextual retrieval adds document context to a chunk’s representation while preserving the original span for citation. Fusion cannot repair authorization, staleness, or poisoning.
variants.prompt: Contextual retrieval prepends document context to each chunk before embedding. What must be preserved separately?
options: The original source span for display, citation, deletion, and audit.
Nothing extra, because the prepended context is part of the chunk now.
Only the embedding, since it is what the retriever actually compares.
optionFeedback: Index-side context improves representations without changing what is cited.
Citing the augmented text would quote words that are not in the source document.
The vector is not what users read, and it cannot be shown in a citation.
variants.hint: What do users and auditors need to see?

variants.title: Use hints honestly
variants.context: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer-shaped passage as a search representation; it must never be cited. Contextual retrieval adds document context to a chunk’s representation while preserving the original span for citation. Fusion cannot repair authorization, staleness, or poisoning.
variants.prompt: Fusion of five lists still returns a stale, unauthorized passage at the top. Can more fusion fix it?
options: Yes, adding more retrieval lists dilutes the bad passage's rank.
Yes, raising the fusion constant flattens the top of every list.
No. Fusion cannot repair authorization, staleness, or poisoning.
optionFeedback: More lists rank the same bad passage, and it sits near the top of each one.
The constant changes weighting, not whether a source is allowed or current.
Fusion orders candidates, while policy and ingestion decide which ones exist.
variants.hint: Which controls handle authorization and freshness?
variants.explanation: Fusion cannot repair a source that policy should have excluded.
